But the reality is that normal isn’t something that returns on its own. It’s something we build back, one action at a time. Each time we vote, show up to a protest, call our representatives, or just talk to another person in our community about what is being done to our country, we are doing our part to build the future we want to live in, even when we can’t see the results of our efforts right away. As hard as it is to live through this constant back and forth, we have to remember that the progress we are fighting for was never going to happen all at once, and not all of us will get to see everything we are working toward become a reality. Some of this work is for the generation after us, and the one after that. But that’s always been true. The women who marched for suffrage didn’t all live to see the 19th Amendment. Year 2: Ally Level
Deepen your education, amplify Black voices, and learn how to leverage privilege for advocacy.

Year 3: Accomplice Level
Use your privilege to actively fight racism and injustice through real action.

I came here LEGALLY in 2022 on an F-1 visa and went to college, graduated then got the OPT work visa (2023-2024) where I worked and paid taxes to the US. 

I married my husband in 2024. And applied for a family based green card as a spouse of an American citizen.

November 2025 I spent 9 days in detention, where I experienced severe neglect of my medical needs, I could have easily lost my life.

I’m type 1 diabetic and my condition was ignored for several days resulting in a blood sugar of 508. I was heading into DKA.
I developed infections requiring antibiotics, but never received them. 

I spent 5 days in isolation which was nothing less than psychological torture. Alone in a cell smaller than a parking spot. I was allowed 1 shower in 5 days. 

After getting out I found out my credit card was also stolen by an employee at the Detention Center and used while I was there. I have other videos about this, and proof. 

NOBODY should go through what I did, and I will continue to fight for what’s right.
I will continue to share my story for those who are too scared to speak up. One day there will be apologies and settlements. 

Please follow along to support and never stop caring for one another!

My case was terminated in court, months later. I had filed the necessary paperwork with USCIS in 2024 and I have no criminal record. In fact, only about 5% in ice detention has a criminal record.

I was detained with women from all over the world. Canada, Australia, the UK, Spain, Mexico, Japan, Romania and other countries. None of us have any criminal history. But even if we had, this is unconstitutional and unacceptable.

HOW TO HELP:
1.  Donate to cover legal fees, litigation, therapy, and other recovery costs. Link in bio.
2.  Follow and support survivors. Share their stories and amplify their voices.
3.  Giving survivors a platform matters. Public attention can make retaliation less likely.
4.  Vote, and demand change from your representatives.
Call, email, show up.

[{'caption': '10/25/26 – As many of you have now read, Duncan Crabtree-Ireland, the head of SAG-AFTRA, reportedly secured a salary increase of 10% to 15% and a contract extension through 2032. According to sources inside the union, these changes were pushed through without appearing on the original agenda.

SAG-AFTRA members, you need to seriously ask yourselves whether your hard-earned dues are being used to represent your interests or enrich union leadership.

There are mechanisms to remove board members and leadership, depending on your union’s constitution and bylaws. There are also potential legal remedies under Title V, Section 501(b) of the Labor-Management Reporting and Disclosure Act, which allows qualifying members to pursue legal action for breaches of fiduciary duty.

I am actively working to identify attorneys willing to speak with members about their legal rights and options.

And to independent production companies, a serious warning: Before placing a production security deposit with SAG-AFTRA, understand the financial risks. Multiple producers have raised allegations of prolonged delays and difficulties recovering their deposits. Until these concerns are adequately addressed, you should not assume your money will be returned promptly or without dispute.

Stay tuned. I will continue investigating these allegations, pursuing accountability, and working to connect union members with attorneys who can explain their legal options.', 'datetime': '2026-10-25T00:00:00.000Z', 'id': '4015917246369825240', 'image_url': 'https://scontent-dfw5-2.cdninstagram.com/v/t51.82787-15/863535101_17908618803566504_5002458218665113490_n.jpg?stp=dst-jpg_e35_s640x640_tt6&_nc_cat=107&ccb=7-5&_nc_sid=18de74&efg=eyJlZmdfdGFnIjoiQ0xJUFMuYmVzdF9pbWFnZV91cmxnZW4uQzMifQ%3D%3D&_nc_ohc=9b7p3Y8Z8CkQ7kNvwEwKnui&_nc_oc=AdqPqo9Uv0I3CHvPGWHsVMytHpYaqOZ353ahiVEkTPELg8w1O8lStU4DZqlvzioEu40&_nc_zt=23&_nc_ht=scontent-dfw5-2.cdninstagram.com&_nc_gid=5tc7EKZTZKRAI5bWrKrJ4Q&_nc_ss=7a689&oh=00_AQR_Ba2UjokiiWljkR7eMq4pECHCseNZDG67svv2x7eR7w&oe=6AED3E8F', 'post_hashtags': None, 'content_type': 'Video', 'url': 'https://www.instagram.com/p/De7Z3VVPQHY'}, {'caption': 'Hollywood’s independent filmmakers have some of the most powerful stories to tell about America… stories of freedom, creativity, resilience, and the American dream.

I’m proposing that the U.S. government, through the U.S. Agency for Global Media and Voice of America, invest in acquiring independent American films and short series for international distribution. Utah has a coal plant that was never allowed to die. The coal units at the Intermountain Power Project near Delta stopped running last year when new gas units took over, so the lights never went out. On November 4, a committee picks that buyer from four secret bids. Every bidder signed a nondisclosure agreement, and state officials confirmed to lawmakers that the public can’t see a single offer. The state gets the final say, and it can even buy the coal units itself with your money.

Who wants a 40-year-old coal plant? At least one data center developer in Delta has said publicly it wants these units to power a giant AI campus. That campus has one small tenant and is hunting for big ones. If no big customer shows up, nobody restarts the coal.

One of the biggest things that moved me away from the Republican Party was realizing how many truly pro-life policies they oppose.

I also created an “alternate cover” that’s a little more intimate, depicting a man and his child watching as a Talisman’s silver rings return to sacred ground overlooking a hazy canyon. Elsewhere, the gatefold illustration shows four colossal Talisman monuments relaying bolts of energy to open a dimensional rift. Another illustration, “Giant Under The Sun”, is a tribute to Chris Squire, featuring a humpback whale rejoicing before a massive oceanic Talisman.

Late in the process, I decided to have some fun bridging the ancient and modern eras of interdimensional reality, so I created an archival photograph of an early 20th Century explorer’s discovery of a Talisman while it’s partially exposed by melting ice, adapting a public domain photograph by Herbert G. Ponting, circa 1911.

One final note: every composition in this sleeve was modeled, composited, or digitally hand-drawn by me, except for the aforementioned Ponting photo. None of the illustrations were created using AI. However, I used Photoshop’s generative tools to clean-up and composite some of the CG renders.

Thank you to everyone at Mercury Studios for gifting me with the rare privilege of working on this special edition of Symphonic Live, and to Jordan Berliant for initially commissioning my work back in 2001-2002. I’m especially grateful for the support of the Yes fan community.”

The Co-Chairs of the European Conservatives and Reformists (ECR) Group in the European Parliament have condemned the Tusk government’s actions against Poland’s Constitutional Tribunal as a violation of the rule of law. They expressed support for President Karol Nawrocki’s defence of the constitutional order and warned European institutions against ignoring these developments.

ECR Co-Chair Nicola Procaccini said:

“The Tusk government’s actions constitute a clear and grave violation of the rule of law. We condemn this attack on judicial independence and Poland’s constitutional safeguards. No government stands above the law.”

“We support President Nawrocki in defending Poland’s constitutional order. The European institutions must not avert their eyes from what is happening. Respect for national sovereignty and judicial independence must remain a matter of principle, unaffected by political alliances.”

ECR Co-Chair Patryk Jaki said:

“Yesterday, Tusk’s left-liberal government used the police to forcibly install its own people, posing as judges, in the independent Constitutional Tribunal. It then had the police block access for the legitimate judges.

You are tired, the work is heavy, and the weight of raising someone else can make the hours feel longer than they are. Yet those same days are moving faster than they appear. While you are counting the minutes until bedtime, your children are quietly growing into people who will one day need you less.

There will come a season when the little hands that once reached for you at every turn no longer reach as often. The questions slow down. The dependence softens. The years that once felt impossible to get through will suddenly look short from the other side. What felt exhausting in the moment becomes the story you will wish you could live one more time.

So stay present in the long days. Even the ones that leave you drained. Even the ones that test your patience. Those ordinary, difficult hours are the ones that will matter most when the house grows quieter. The next generation does not need perfect parents. It needs fathers and mothers who understand that the work is short and the memory is long.

If you are ready to hear more about how to lead a family through these fleeting seasons, the full conversations are waiting on To My Sons and Daughters Podcast. Long story short… The PACT Act was a law signed by Biden on 8/10/22 and is viewed as the most significant expansion of VA benefits in decades. It’s short for Sergeant First Class (SFC) Health Robinson Honoring Our Promise to Address Comprehensive Toxics Act of 2022. 

It provides new and expanded benefits for Vets (and their survivors) exposed to burn pits and other toxic substances. Benefits of the PACT Act include: 
- Expanded access to VA health care 
- New and expanded presumptive conditions
- Increased compensation for service-connected disabilities
- New and expanded benefits for survivors. 

The VA offers a simple and easy to read visual to understand which route to apply is best for you (or your loved one). Check our link in bio to access this doc!

If you, or a veteran, family member, or survivor would like more information about the PACT Act and your VA Benefits, start with one of these options: 
- Visit the online portal, create an account and ask questions: ask.VA.gov 
- Call for 24/7/365 help: 1-800-MyVA411 
- Walk-In to your local care provider: VA.gov/find/locations 
- Ask your local VA org for help (VA.gov/disability/get-help-filing-claim) 
Check the New Health Care & Benefits Map provided by the VA: https://www.va.gov/files/2023-02/Journey%20Map_Accessing%20VA%20Benefits%2C%20Services%20V2.28.2023%201530hrs_2.pdf

- The process can take months or years. The sooner you start, the sooner you will receive your benefits.
- You may lose your backpay if you delay. The VA pays backpay to vets from the date of their injury or illness to the date their claim is approved. 
- Your medical records may become more difficult to obtain. 
- Your condition may worsen over time. This could make it more difficult to prove your disability.

#2 - Prepare your documentation
Don't skip getting a medical opinion, it can help strengthen your case
- Make a copy of your DD-214 (Certificate of Release or Discharge from Active Duty)
- Collect all relevant medical records, both military and civilian
- Gather a statement from a medical professional or other expert attesting to the nature and severity of your disability (Don’t forget about mental health claims if needed, your brain health matters too)

#3 - Common Mistakes and how to avoid them
Mistakes
- Incomplete, insufficient and/or incorrect docs
- Missing deadlines 
- Lack of medical evidence
- Quitting after your claim is denied

How to avoid them
- Incomplete, insufficient and/or incorrect docs
- Missing deadlines 
- Lack of medical evidence
- Quitting after your claim is denied

#4 - Seek professional assistance
Services
- Helping you to understand which benefits you are eligible for
- Helping you gather and organize your evidence
- Reviewing your claim form and providing feedback
- Representing you before the VA during the claims process
- Appealing a denied claim

Benefits
- Increase chances of success
- Reduced stress 
- More time for you to focus on your health and well-being

#5 - Dealing with denials 
- File a Notice of Disagreement (NOD): An NOD is a formal request to the VA to review its decision. 
- Request a Decision Review Officer (DRO) review: A DRO is a VA employee who reviews denied claims and makes recommendations on whether to approve or deny them. 
- Appeal to the Board of Veterans Appeals (BVA): The BVA is a panel of three judges who review denied claims. 
- File a new claim: If you have new evidence, you can file a new claim

[{'caption': '🚨 You can report an insurance company to your state’s Insurance Commissioner. And more people need to know this.

When an insurance company denies medically necessary care, delays payment, mishandles a claim, or engages in potentially unfair practices, you don’t have to simply accept the decision.

You can file a complaint with your state’s Insurance Commissioner — the government office responsible for regulating insurance companies and investigating certain consumer complaints.

What can happen when you file a complaint?

➡️ The insurer may be required to respond to the complaint.
➡️ The state may review whether the company followed applicable insurance laws and regulations.
➡️ The investigation may uncover a pattern of unfair practices.
➡️ Depending on the circumstances, the regulator may take further action.

⚠️ Filing a complaint does NOT guarantee that a denial will be overturned or that your claim will be paid. But it creates a formal record and gives regulators an opportunity to examine what happened.

And here’s what I want patients to understand: An insurance company’s decision is not automatically the final word on your healthcare.

Document what happened. Keep your denial letters. Save your correspondence. Understand your appeal rights. And when appropriate, file a complaint.

As a physician and an independent medical practice owner, I believe patients deserve to know that they have options when the system fails them.

Insurance companies should be held accountable to the laws that govern them.

📣 Share this with someone who has ever been told, “Your insurance won’t cover it.”

This map reveals how the familiar Mercator projection significantly distorts the size of countries, especially near the poles. Areas like Greenland, Canada, and Russia appear much larger than they truly are, while regions closer to the equator—such as Africa and South America—often look smaller than their real size.

By comparing true land areas (shown in red outlines) to their Mercator depiction (in blue), the map highlights these dramatic differences. For example, Greenland looks nearly the size of Africa on many maps, but in reality, Africa is about 14 times larger.

How the Override Process Works

• Constitutional Rule: Under Article I, Section 7 of the U.S. Constitution, a regular veto can be overridden only by a two-thirds vote in both the House of Representatives and the Senate.

• Chamber Sequence: The chamber where the bill originated votes first. If it fails to reach the two-thirds threshold, the bill dies and the other chamber does not vote. If it passes with two-thirds, it moves to the second chamber.

• Outcome: If both chambers achieve a two-thirds majority, the bill becomes law without the President’s signature.

• The High Bar: A two-thirds supermajority requires at least 290 votes in the House (out of 435) and 67 votes in the Senate (out of 100), meaning the opposing party must win over a significant number of members from the President’s party.

• Regular Veto: The President returns the unsigned bill with a memorandum of disapproval to the originating house of Congress within 10 days. This type can be overridden by Congress.

• Pocket Veto: If the President receives a bill and does not sign it within 10 days, and Congress has adjourned during that period—preventing the President from returning it—the bill dies. Pocket vetoes cannot be overridden because Congress is not in session to vote.

Today is National Truth & Reconciliation day, a day to meant to recognize the horrific traumas of Canada’s genocide and ongoing disposition of Indigenous peoples. Given the white nationalist gathering at Kamloops Indian Residential School, I felt compelled to share some images I made there a number of years ago.

For over a century, the Canadian state worked with the Catholic Church to forcefully separate children from their families. These children were re-educated, malnourished, tortured, abused, and many died. The sites of these atrocities are still standing. You needn’t just look overseas or to the history books to see Canada’s participation in colonization.

The white nationalists who gathered at Kamloops are not a fluke, they are the result of an ongoing attempt to delegitimization the violent history of Canadian colonialism and Residential Schools. This viewpoint has morphed from a fringe far right opinion into a commonly held idea among “common sense” conservatives. It is not enough to ignore or consider such thinking as fringe, it must be challenged clearly and swiftly for the survivors and the victims.

We cannot be tempted by forgetfulness. These actions were undertaken by men and women, we cannot forget the feeling of hatred this history makes us feel; we cannot forget the sacrifice. To paraphrase Walter Benjamin’s Theses on The Philosophy of History, these wish to correct this history is nourished by the image of enslaved ancestors rather than that of liberated grandchildren.

We find the remnants of this genocidal legacy in the ground, air, and waters surrounding us. It is a history has not yet been reconciled for.

These images were shot on 800 iso film, meaning they could only be overexposed. In a technical sense, this would be the wrong situation to shoot this kind of extremely light sensitive film. I believe it is the perfect situation to shoot this film stock; to overexpose images of underexposed history.
